trials.name: Footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: Keeps the baseline body. For each brick type it max- and mean-pools learned cell features over the brick's own footprint (dy x dx) and feeds them to that type's logit. This makes it easy to learn 'all footprint cells are missing at the same landing layer' and the max height under the footprint, so 2x1, 1x2 and 2x2 placements should be learned faster. It is refuted if the 4-seed mean is not above the baseline's.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HID = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList(
            [nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + 2 * HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        c = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, av], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: Reshapes the build, target, missing and extra channels into a [4, Z, Y, X] volume, adds the height, time and layer-index planes, and applies a 3x3x3 Conv3d. One set of weights then handles every layer, so the rule 'this cell is missing and the cell below is filled' is learned once instead of Z times, which should help with few samples. import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
C3 = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv3d(8, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.mix = nn.Conv2d(C3 * self.Z, WIDTH, 1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vol = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].reshape(B, 3, 1, Y, X).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.arange(Z, dtype=obs.dtype, device=obs.device) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        v = torch.cat([vol, planes, zc], dim=1)
        h = torch.relu(self.conv3(v))
        h = h.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)
        f = torch.relu(self.mix(h))
        f = torch.relu(self.conv2(f))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HEADS = 4
HID = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        n = int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X)
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, n, WIDTH) * 0.02)
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 3 * WIDTH)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(WIDTH)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(WIDTH, 2 * WIDTH), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH))
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + 2 * HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        for h in list(self.type_heads) + [self.done_head]:
            nn.init.orthogonal_(h.weight, gain=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(h.bias)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        f = self.body(obs)
        N = Y * X
        D = WIDTH // HEADS
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        h = self.ln1(t)
        qkv = self.qkv(h).reshape(B, N, 3, HEADS, D).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
        att = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(D), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(att, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, WIDTH)
        t = t + self.proj(o)
        t = t + self.mlp(self.ln2(t))
        f = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, WIDTH, Y, X)
        c = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for ti, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[ti](torch.cat([f, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

For each brick type, a learned softmax over layers (computed from footprint-max-pooled cell features) estimates where the brick lands. The head then reads per-layer features, min- and mean-pooled over the footprint, at that layer. This follows the task's rule: a good placement fills only missing cells at its landing layer. r≈1.25. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
C3 = 16
HID = 16


def fp_max(x, dy, dx):
    return F.max_pool2d(F.pad(x, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1)), (dy, dx), stride=1)


def fp_avg(x, dy, dx):
    return F.avg_pool2d(F.pad(x, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1)), (dy, dx), stride=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.c3a = nn.Conv3d(8, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3b = nn.Conv3d(C3, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.mix = nn.Conv2d(C3 * self.Z, WIDTH, 1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.hcell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.land = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, self.Z, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + 2 * C3, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        for h in list(self.type_heads) + [self.done_head]:
            nn.init.orthogonal_(h.weight, gain=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(h.bias)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vol = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].reshape(B, 3, 1, Y, X).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.arange(Z, dtype=obs.dtype, device=obs.device) / max(Z - 1, 1)
        zc = zc.reshape(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        vin = torch.cat([vol, planes, zc], dim=1)
        v = torch.relu(self.c3a(vin))
        v = v + torch.relu(self.c3b(v))
        vf = v.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)
        f = torch.relu(self.mix(vf))
        f = f + torch.relu(self.conv2(f))
        hc = torch.relu(self.hcell(f))
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = torch.softmax(self.land[t](fp_max(hc, dy, dx)), dim=1).unsqueeze(1)
            vmin = (-fp_max(-vf, dy, dx)).reshape(B, C3, Z, Y, X)
            vmean = fp_avg(vf, dy, dx).reshape(B, C3, Z, Y, X)
            smin = (vmin * p).sum(2)
            smean = (vmean * p).sum(2)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](torch.cat([f, smin, smean], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: r3c1 + global context broadcast
trials.hypothesis: Adds one change to r3c1: the network pools features over the whole board, passes them through a small MLP, and adds the result back to every cell's features before the placement head, with near-zero extra FLOPs. Each placement logit then knows what is left to build across the whole board, which matters for build order (do not seal a cell that is still missing) and for weighing placements against DONE. This was the aim of r2c2's attention block, but without its cost. Refuted if its 4-seed mean is not above r3c1's.

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HID = 32
BLOCKS = 2
GW = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GW), nn.ReLU())
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(GW, WIDTH)
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList(
            [nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + 2 * HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GW, 1)
        for h in list(self.type_heads) + [self.done_head]:
            nn.init.orthogonal_(h.weight, gain=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(h.bias)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = torch.relu(self.stem(obs))
        for conv in self.blocks:
            f = f + torch.relu(conv(f))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = torch.relu(f + self.bcast(g).unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))
        c = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(cp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](torch.cat([f, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, so this round tests three directions against the starting architecture. Training runs only 131k steps, so learning speed per sample probably matters more than raw capacity, and each candidate stays close to the baseline's compute (r ≤ 1.2). What the task needs: for each brick type and anchor, the network must work out the landing layer (the highest build height under the footprint) and check whether every cell the brick would fill is a missing target cell. The baseline infers this from a 5x5 receptive field and has to learn it separately for every layer channel. The candidates are: (1) a placement head that pools learned features over each brick's footprint, (2) a 3D-conv stem that shares weights across layers, and (3) a deeper residual body at the same compute. If two seeds differ a lot, read that as seed luck rather than a real effect.
analyses.2: I can't see any scores, so round 1 tells me only that all three ideas run safely inside the compute and time limits (r of 1.05 to 1.17). Footprint pooling, a layer-shared 3D stem and residual depth are all untested on success. The final pick uses real dev scores from the top 3 trials, so this round goes for the highest expected score rather than clean single-variable tests. The three candidates are: (1) all three round-1 ideas combined, (2) global self-attention, since a 5x5 receptive field on an 8x8 grid may limit decisions about ordering and DONE, (3) a structured head that learns a soft landing layer for each footprint and reads per-layer 3D features at that layer, matching what the task needs. Each candidate also uses small-gain initialisation on the policy outputs, the standard PPO practice, which keeps the starting policy close to uniform. All stay at r ≤ 1.6 to keep most of the training steps.
analyses.3: All six trials trained without errors, but scores are hidden, so I have to choose using priors and cost. The most useful number we can see is the compute ratio. All three round-2 candidates came out near r≈2, much higher than I estimated, so each trained on only about 65k steps. That halving of training could hide any gain from their features. Cheap networks get the full 131k steps for free. This round therefore keeps every candidate near r≈1 while still adding the ideas suited to this task: footprint pooling (for multi-cell bricks and the max height under a footprint), extra depth with residual connections (for computing landing layers), and a 3D stem that shares weights across layers. The three candidates are: (1) a refinement combining residual depth with the footprint head at r≈1.05; (2) a new idea, a deep, wide depthwise-separable network whose receptive field covers the whole grid at r<1; (3) the round-2 combo shrunk to r≈1.2, to test whether halved training steps were what held it back.
analyses.4: Scores are hidden, so the evidence is only compute and correctness. All trials ran. FLOPs ratios often came out higher than estimated (the depthwise network was described as r<1 but measured 2.57; the landing-layer head was estimated at 1.25 but measured 1.95). The ~2x combos trained on half the steps or less, which is risky. The cheap designs (r 1.05–1.2) keep about 120k steps and are safer for the final 4-seed selection. Of these, r3c1 (residual width-48 body plus footprint-pooled head) combines both round-1 ideas at r=1.09. In the last round I refine r3c1 with one change each, keeping r near 1: (1) more depth at lower width, (2) cheap whole-board context passed back to every cell, for build order and DONE, at almost no FLOPs, (3) dilated blocks so the network sees the whole grid at the same cost. Each candidate is refuted if its 4-seed mean is not above r3c1's.
